afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 290551
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1051 PM MST Wed Oct 28 2026

.UPDATE...Updated 06Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Tranquil weather conditions will continue through Thursday with 
temperatures within a few degrees of daily normals.

- An unsettled weather pattern will return to the region Friday 
through Sunday resulting in much cooler temperatures and enhanced 
chances for widespread rainfall.

- Embedded thunderstorms and heavier rainfall may affect some areas 
resulting in localized minor flooding, specifically Friday and 
Sunday. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Thursday/... 
Semi quasi-zonal aloft continues over the region today and will
shift out of the southwest starting Thursday. Both directions 
will keep calm weather, dry conditions, and near normal 
temperatures over the region today and Thursday, while the next 
weather system is at the doorstep of the region and is expected to
impact the region as early as Friday morning. Until then, as 
previously mentioned, quiet weather is expected. Heights aloft are
near the NAEFS climatological average for late October, resulting
in near to slightly above afternoon highs, with today's highs in 
the mid 80s, and tomorrow the western lower deserts will remain in
the mid 80s, while south- central AZ will be 1-2 degrees warmer, 
in the mid to upper 80s. Ahead of the aforementioned weather 
system, PWATs will begin to gradually increase as subtropical 
moisture will begin to be advected northward into the region, 
increasing PWATs from 100-130% of normal to to 200-220% of normal 
by Thursday night. This will lead to increasing in cloud coverage 
over the course of Thursday. This increase in cloud coverage in 
combination of the warmer temperatures will lead to Friday
overnight and morning's low temperatures 5-7 degrees above 
normal. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Friday through Tuesday/... 
Forecast confidence is increasing for two separate weather events, 
Friday through Sunday, both of which could bring impactful rain 
amounts to portions of central Arizona. The increasing moisture on 
Thursday into Friday is expected to peak during the daytime hours 
Friday with PWATs reaching 225-250% of normals and low level mixing 
ratios of 8-9 g/kg, centered over Maricopa and Pinal Counties. 
Forecast soundings show the moisture will be quite deep, extending 
fairly evenly throughout the column with modest elevated MUCAPE up 
to around 500 J/kg. Strong jet forced ascent is also seen moving 
over the area on Friday combining with the modest southerly low 
level upslope ascent. 

Showers are expected to begin developing a few hours after midnight 
Thursday night before increasing in coverage and intensity by around 
sunrise Friday. Both the GEFS and EPS show QPF maxima centered from 
Phoenix to around the Tonto NF with amounts averaging 0.50-0.75". 
Considering the available instability and steep mid-level lapse 
rates, we should expect scattered thunderstorms too, mostly embedded 
with the shower activity. General rainfall rates are likely to 
mostly fall within a 0.05-0.20" range, but it would not be 
surprising to see very localized rates of around 1" per hour within 
any thunderstorms. These higher rainfall rates should pose a minor 
flood threat on Friday, mainly affecting area washes and the typical 
unbridged low water crossings. There is potential for higher 
rainfall amounts with the NBM 75th percentile showing amounts 
between 1.50-2.00" centered over the foothills just north of 
Phoenix. A Slight Risk for excessive rainfall remains on the updated 
WPC ERO and based on the model run-to-run consistency, Flood Watches 
are likely to be needed for at least north-central and northeast 
Maricopa County. The shower and thunderstorm activity should also 
extend eastward into Gila County later on Friday before quickly 
winding down Friday evening as we lose upper level support. 

The large scale trough will remain positioned along and into the 
Western U.S. into Saturday with the main low center near the Pacific 
Northwest, but another strong shortwave diving into the base of the 
trough is expected to help bring another low developing off the 
coast of California Saturday night into Sunday. Saturday is expected 
to be mostly a dry day, but there will still likely be some isolated 
upslope type showers mostly focused over the high terrain north and 
east of Phoenix. However, this will just be the calm in between 
weather systems with the second one moving in starting late Saturday 
night expected to be stronger and more impactful.

By Saturday evening, guidance shows a strong atmospheric river (AR) 
starting to make its way into northern Baja and far southern 
California. By Sunday morning, the full force of this AR is expected 
to be directed at southern Arizona and northern Sonora Mexico with 
PWATs increasing to 275-325% of normal, or right near record levels 
for our area this time of year. Compared to model runs 24 hours ago, 
the latest depicts even better moisture and a stronger system. Upper 
level forced ascent should begin to increase over our area by 
Saturday night, coinciding with increasing low and mid level upslope 
south southwesterly flow.

A large area of light to moderate rain is likely to develop ahead of 
the approaching weather system late Saturday night into early Sunday 
affecting the bulk of the region, particularly central and eastern 
Arizona. Although model uncertainty is decreasing, there is still a 
good deal of uncertainty in expected rainfall amounts. This looks to 
be a longer duration light to moderate rain event with limited 
instability keeping rainfall rates under 0.50" per hour and even 
lower across the lower deserts. However, because this may end up 
easily being a 6-12 hour rain event, the rainfall could quickly add 
up, especially into the higher terrain northeast of Phoenix where 
upslope forcing will be maximized. The latest NBM QPF shows a wide 
range of potential amounts with averages around 1" in the Phoenix 
area to upwards of 1.50-2.00" over the high terrain northeast of 
Phoenix. The lower end of the forecast shows amounts closer to 0.50" 
and 1.00-1.50" respectively, but the higher end potential is more 
like 2-3". Considering this will be the second rain event within 3 
days, any additional moderate to heavy rain could compound any 
flooding issues that occur Friday. Rain chances may linger through 
Sunday night across portions of central and eastern Arizona, but by 
mid to late Monday morning, much of the area should be drying out as 
the system is quickly pushes east of the area.

Temperatures during this unsettled weather pattern will fall below 
normal starting Friday with highs dropping to between 75F-80F before 
bottoming out closer to 70F highs for Sunday and/or Monday. It would 
not be out of the question for some lower desert communities stuck 
in prolonged rain Sunday to not even breach the 70F threshold. NBM 
guidance shows fairly large forecast temperature spread for the 
first half of next week as the large scale troughing may linger near 
the region with depressed H5 heights for a couple more days. If this 
happens, highs will very slowly creep upward through the low to mid 
70s, whereas if the ridge quickly takes over, highs closer to 80F 
would be more common by next Tuesday or Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0550Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT; 
No major weather issues will exist through early Friday morning.
Wind behavior will be similar to the past 24 hours. Another 
extended period of mid/late afternoon south cross runway winds 
(140v240) is expected around the Phoenix metro before becoming W 
in the evening. Extended periods of light and variable to nearly
calm conditions will be common. 

Dry conditions are expected through the next 24 hours. Around or
shortly before sunrise on Friday morning showers and storms are
expected start popping up in/around the Phoenix Metro. Due to 
this VCTS has been introduced into the KPHX TAF with this package 
beginning at 11Z Friday. With this activity CIGs will lower to 
around 5-8 kft, CIGs as low as 3-4 kft are expected with any 
shower or storm activity. Any heavy rainfall would also lead to 
lower VIS. 
 
Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

No major weather issues will exist through Thursday night under 
periods of increasing thick cirrus decks. Wind behavior will be 
similar to the past 24 hours. KIPL will see winds fluctuate 
between S/SE and W. Current N winds at KBLH will go S late 
tomorrow morning and then SW tomorrow evening. Winds speeds will 
be aob 7 kt. Although, extended periods of nearly calm conditions 
will be common.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Dry conditions with near normal temperatures will persist through 
Thursday under increasing cloud cover. Minimum humidity levels
through Thursday will fall into a 20-40% range following fair to 
good overnight recovery of 40-60%. Starting Friday. and through 
the weekend, MinRH's will increase substantially with widespread 
50-80%, due to several days of unsettled weather, bringing 
widespread rainfall, and cooler temperatures. Otherwise, winds 
will remain unseasonably light with minimal upslope breeziness.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Ryan 
LONG TERM...Kuhlman/18 
AVIATION...Berislavich 
FIRE WEATHER...Ryan/Kuhlman
